<reason>CON built the sharpest structural frame of the debate: strip out the individually actionable content (addresses, schools, explicit intimidation) and the motion's unique territory is the "blank case," where coordination is only inferred from volume, timing and a shared target — so the motion attaches the harshest, fastest remedy to the weakest evidence, and the brigade detector is itself brigadable. That frame, plus the calibration answer to PRO's Q1 (throttling is proportionate to a guess, suspension is not) and the extracted concession that review must precede suspension, gave CON a genuinely live route. But PRO answered the two decisive pressure points more successfully than CON answered PRO's. PRO's reading of "immediate" as describing the trigger (act on coordination now, in hours, rather than waiting for an explicit threat) is a plausible, honest defense that keeps the motion intact. More damagingly, PRO's Pressure Q2 forced CON into the debate's weakest move: calling "hope she's home tonight" intimidation "on its face" and treating forty such posts as forty independent content violations. PRO's closing crystallized the dilemma cleanly — that sentence carries no threat and no artifact, and CON only reaches it by reading it through the surrounding campaign, which is precisely suspension for posts that are not explicitly threatening. CON's patch (context-reading of the speaker's own words is still content) is a fair distinction but concedes the motion's operative language. CON also never squarely handled "nice porch," the cleanest example of a non-artifact, non-threat post that is only legible through coordination, so the "no unique territory" claim did not fully land. PRO also gave a workable decider test ("is this about what he did, or about where he sleeps?") that blunted the boycott/#MeToo/warehouse-workers slippage, while keeping the reversibility asymmetry alive against throttling, which leaves participants posting at an already-doxxed target. Close and competent on both sides; PRO's edge is real but narrow.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Q2 followed by its closing: forced CON to either let forty non-artifact "hope she's home tonight" posts stand or admit it suspends for facially innocuous sentences read through the surrounding campaign — which PRO then showed is the motion itself. CON's best counterpunch, that severity must match confidence and throttling survives a wrong guess, kept the round close but did not resolve the "nice porch" residue.</best_rebuttal>
